entries.title: Isaiah 45:1
segments:
Anointed; as set apart to the work of redeeming God's people. 
 
  The gates shall not be shut; remarkably fulfulled in the conquest of Babylon, the gates of the city having been left open during a night of feasting.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:4
segments: Hast not known me; when Cyrus took Babylon he was ignorant of Jehovah and of the designs which he purposed to accomplish through him, and was only indulging his own ambitious desires.  The knowledge which he afterwards had of God,

, was doubtless received from the Jews residing in Babylon. 
 
God has often employed heathen princes, who were ignorant of him and his counsels, to accomplish wonderful deliverances for his people.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:7
segments: Since God is the author of all things, he governs and sets limits to all.  The good and bad actions of men and angels are so under his control that he accomplishes through them his own wise counsels, while they are left altogether free and responsible to him for their conduct.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:8
segments:
Drop down; distil. 
 
  Open; open her bosom to send forth a harvest of righteousness and salvation. 
 
  Let them bring forth; that is, the heavens and the skies.  God's righteousness and salvation are here compared to refreshing showers and a harvest of precious fruits.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:9
segments:
vv 9-10. 
 
  Woe unto him; God rebukes his people for arraigning his dealings with them at the bar of their own reason.  The primary reference may be to their long-continued sufferings during the Babylonish captivity; but the words have a general application to God's treatment of all men in all ages. 
 
All our capacity to reason concerning God's works and ways is his gift. How unspeakable the folly and wickedness of contending against his dealings with us; as if the creature could sit in judgment on the infinite Creator.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:11
segments: Command ye me; in the way of petitioning, not of prescribing.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:14
segments:
Labor; wealth gained by labor. 
 
  Men of stature; the Ethiopians and Sabeans were celebrated for their tallness. 
 
  Shall come after thee--make supplication unto thee; compare
.  These passages are to be understood in a spiritual sense.  The meaning is, that God will give his church, through Christ, universal dominion and honor.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:15
segments: Hidest thyself; hidest thy counsels in darkness.  The prophet has in mind the sore afflictions through which Zion must come to the fulfilment of the promises which he has just recorded.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:18
segments: Not in vain; as God's purpose in creating the earth shall be fulfilled, so shall all his counsels respecting his chosen people.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:19
segments:
In secret, in a dark place of the earth; not uttering dark responses from caves, like the ancient oracles. 
 
  In vain; as did those who consulted the heathen oracles. 
 
The many and explicit predictions of God's word constitute a proof of its divine origin, such as no pretended revelation can offer.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:20
segments: Escaped of the nations; the remnant of them who have escaped God's judgments.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:21
segments:
Tell ye; recount your arguments. 
 
  Them; the patrons of idols. 
 
  Declared this; deliverance of my people through Cyrus, which I have foretold. 
 
  From that time; see note on

entries.title: Isaiah 45:23
segments: God possesses absolute authority over all men: and he will exercise it throughout eternity, for their salvation if righteous; but if wicked, for their destruction.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:24
segments: It is vain to look for justifying righteousness, or strength to overcome sin, to any thing that we can do, or that our fellow sinners can do for us.  We must receive both from God as his free gift through Jesus Christ.
